children: By Margot Patrick and Michael Hennessey
Partners Group shares tumbled Tuesday after the Swiss asset manager reported falling revenue and named new leadership to steady it through a turbulent stretch for private markets.

Chief Executive David Layton is stepping down at the end of the year to become chief investment officer and chairman of the global investment committee, the company said. The new co-CEOs will be longtime executives Roberto Cagnati and Juri Jenkner, who have both been at Partners Group for more than 20 years.
Shares were down around 7% in European trading on Tuesday. The stock has fallen 31% year to date.

In a first-half earnings update, Partners Group said performance-fee income was sharply lower from a year ago, reflecting a more-limited market for exiting the companies and stakes it buys for private equity and debt funds. That pushed overall revenue lower, even though management fees grew along with the pot of assets managed by the company.

Partners Group has been under pressure this year as clients soured on private markets and investors grew concerned over its exposure to software and healthcare businesses. In June, it capped redemptions from a flagship private-markets fund because of high demand from investors to get their money back.

"Our exit pipeline remains full, and while some exit processes are likely to shift into 2027, our mid- to long-term guidance remains for performance income to be around 25%-40% of total revenue in the years ahead," said Layton, the departing chief. In the first-half of 2026, the figure was around 19%, and Layton said it should end up at around 20%-25% for the full year.

Layton had been co-CEO since 2019 and became CEO in 2021. He is mainly based in the group's U.S. headquarters outside Denver. The new co-CEOs, Jenkner and Cagnati, are both at Swiss headquarters in Zug.

The company backed its expectations of total new client assets between $26 billion and $32 billion for the full year. Assets under management at the end of the first half stood at $186 billion, up from $174.4 billion a year before.
